claims.text: The initial W–Cu composite contains W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix.
The initial W–Cu composite typically exhibits phase separation.
The initial W–Cu composite typically contains interfacial voids.
High-temperature diffusion bonding followed by controlled cooling will reduce phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
High-temperature diffusion bonding followed by controlled cooling will reduce void formation at W–Cu interfaces.
The treatment will enhance bonding at W–Cu interfaces.
Diffusion bonding promotes atomic intermixing at the W–Cu interface.
Interfacial atomic intermixing reduces phase separation.
Reduced void content and phase separation improve interface continuity.
Improved interface continuity reduces thermal resistance.
The treated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than the untreated composite under relevant heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The proposed process is performed above the melting point of Cu and below the melting point of W.
The proposed process requires an inert atmosphere.
The hypothesis is not applicable if excessive melting or grain growth occurs.

contradictions.description: The intervention is called solid-state diffusion bonding, but the specified processing temperature is above the Cu melting point, so the Cu constituent would not remain solid.

The required processing window explicitly exceeds the Cu melting point, while the boundary excludes excessive melting without defining how intentional Cu melting is distinguished from disqualifying melting.
